environment: Ubuntu WSL, Go 1.26.0, PostgreSQL 16.14, isolated migration-backed schemas and private temporary files

checks.name: private_create_edit_delete_events
checks.detail: Real mutations and PostgreSQL recipient resolution delivered minimal create/edit/delete hints only to the two participants. A nonparticipant administrator received none; a blocked peer was removed from current recipients. Repeated 10 times.

checks.name: attachment_count_boundary
checks.detail: Ten attachments created ten links; an eleven-attachment send created no message and left the last object unattached. Repeated 10 times.

checks.name: size_reservation_path_and_cleanup
checks.detail: Existing native tests passed for exactly 25,000,000 versus 25,000,001 bytes, 2 GiB/10% reserve and concurrent reservations, filesystem traversal/symlink protection, PostgreSQL hidden-file cleanup and live-link recheck. Cleanup tests repeated 5 times.

checks.name: notification_policy
checks.detail: Three focused frontend files, 10 tests passed for caller-local generic notifications, cross-tab deduplication and realtime refresh.

checks.name: backend_suite
checks.detail: go test -json -count=1 ./... with both PostgreSQL test URL variables: 665 passed, 0 skipped, 0 failed; focused go vet passed.

checks.name: authenticated_http_and_browser
checks.detail: An integrated authenticated HTTP/browser pass must still demonstrate cookie/session ACL and notification delivery on a fixed candidate.

limitations: Synthetic low-disk snapshots prove admission logic but do not measure the deployment attachment volume; that is QA-08.
Unit notification tests do not prove browser permission and delivery on the candidate build.
